summary: Nike released its Q2 2025 earnings report, showing a decline in revenue and net income compared to the previous year. The company reported revenues of $12.4 billion, down 8% on a reported basis, with a similar decline on a currency-neutral basis. Net income also saw a significant drop, reaching $1.2 billion, down 26% from the previous year. Nike's gross margin fell by 100 basis points to 43.6%, attributed to higher discounts and an altered channel mix. Despite these challenges, Nike remains committed to shareholder returns, distributing $1.6 billion through dividends and share repurchases. Nike's management, led by CEO Elliott Hill, is focused on repositioning the business to prioritize sport and enhance shareholder value. The company aims to strengthen its brand and improve financial performance by accelerating portfolio shifts and enhancing operational efficiency. Nike remains committed to long-term growth and shareholder value as it navigates current market challenges.
